thread:
jess: heads up — p99 spiked in lga pop around 12:04 UTC, tails up to ~420ms for short-chat workloads

dave: saw that, p50 mostly fine but p99 jump correlates with increased retransmits on host nets

anita: any noisy neighbor indications? cpu steal or network tx drops?

jess: looking — host metrics show CPU steal ~8% on a handful of hosts, but the bigger signal is tx-queue length on eth0 and multi-ms queuing in ifstat

leo: can you paste the tcpdump/ss output? also which kernel selector was active (fast-path vs safe-path)?

jess: dump attached (snippet):
```
12:04:12.123456 IP hostA > hostB: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 64240
12:04:12.223456 IP hostA > hostB: Flags [P.], seq 513:1024, ack 1, win 64240
```

ifconfig eth0: txqueuelen 1000 -> observed bursts hitting ~900

and runtime profile shows kernel-selector picked "aggressive-opt" kernels for ~60% of requests at that time

anita: aggressive-opt is sensitive to tail latency when host scheduling/egress is noisy — it assumes low NIC backpressure

dave: that explains it. if the NIC queues then batching heuristics and KV cache behavior can amplify tail latency — KV cache misses trigger long KV restoration which funnels into same kernel path

jess: profiling (perf top dump) shows high context-switches and high ms per token when kv-cache miss + aggressive kernel pair used

leo: can we flip those hosts to safe-path kernel heuristic temporarily? config is per-host: `runtime.kernel_selector=conservative`

anita: yes — also lower batch size and increase batch timeout on the hosts to reduce queue buildup: `batch.max_tokens=1024`, `batch.timeout_ms=8`

deploy-bot: rolling config change request queued: runtime.kernel_selector=conservative for hosts lga-pop-0[3-6] — approver: @dave

dave: approved, rolling now. will also apply `kv.cache_eviction_threshold=0.85 -> 0.92` to avoid aggressive evictions during noisy periods

infra-bot: change applied to lga-pop-03, lga-pop-04. Observed immediate drop in tx-queue to <200 and p99 fell ~220ms within 90s

jess: nice — still seeing a couple hosts with high steal, marking them for host drain + debug (suspect noisy tenant VM)

leo: follow-up actions: 1) add kernel-selector signal for nic-queue occupancy so we avoid aggressive-opt when txq > 70% 2) add KV-cache warmup telemetry to identify miss storms 3) run load repro in staging with induced egress queueing to validate heuristics

anita: logging note: add a new debug tag `heuristic.trigger=kernel_switch` and record current TX queue length + batch size when selector flips

dave: will open a tiny RFC for the selector change, but for now keep the conservative flip until hosts are healthy

jess: postmortem / short notes — root cause: noisy neighbor egress queueing on subset of LGA hosts -> aggravated by current kernel-selector + batching heuristics and KV-cache eviction thresholds -> p99 spike. Mitigations: host drain + conservative kernel selector, tune batching, raise eviction threshold, add telemetry for future detection.

leo: thanks team. follow-ups assigned to @jess (drain + repro), @anita (telemetry + RFC), @dave (eviction tuning + ops)

jess: closing thread, will file full incident writeup in incidents channel after drain completes :white_check_mark:
